exposure: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study involved 120 neonates, equally divided between those delivered via cesarean section and those delivered vaginally.
finding: Cesarean delivery is associated with a higher incidence of Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (NRDS) compared to vaginal delivery, with gestational age and antenatal steroid use also significantly influencing the risk.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery is associated with a higher incidence of NRDS (40%) compared to vaginal delivery (31.67%).
gest_age: Neonates born before 37 weeks gestation showed a particularly high incidence of NRDS.
